agent_notes: bil'adai: Radak records two readings of the final yod (plural ending vs. suffix). I rendered 'apart from me' / 'nothing for me' and noted that the BBE 'Give me nothing' is an interpretation. The ruling that those who stayed with the baggage share equally is Rashi's link to 1 Sam 30:24; I cite it as his comment.
'All these' is ambiguous: Radak takes it as the four with the five; Sforno has Amraphel's side making an agreement there. I translated it neutrally and set out both in the commentary.
'beham' (in Ham) could also be read as 'with them'; all five English versions take it as the place Ham, as do the commentators and the Onkelos rendering (a place-name). Followed them.

agent_notes: STEPBible gives 'Hazezon'; the vocalised text is Hatzatzon, and I used the common English form Hazazon-Tamar (cf. 2 Chr 20:2, as cited by Rashi). Anachronism of 'the Amalekite' is handled via Rashi, Ramban and Radak; I did not choose between them.
KJV/Webster 'with' vs ASV/BBE 'against' for 'et': the Hebrew is the same preposition as in 14:2 and 14:8's 'itam'. Literal layer keeps 'with'; dramatic layer uses 'against'.

[event:evt.gen_14.kings_revolt] The chapter gives no absolute link to Abram's own timeline except its place after Gen 13:18 (Abram at Mamre). The twelve years of service began before this chapter's story and cannot be placed. I therefore anchored the revolt (13th year) on the END of evt.gen_13.settles_at_mamre with a 1-year offset and a wide 2-year margin. The offset is a guess: only the order is given by the text. Abram's age is not stated in this chapter (Gen 12:4 puts him at 75 on leaving Haran, Gen 16:3 at 85 ten years later), so no birth-anchor offset is used.

[event:evt.gen_14.eastern_campaign] The campaign (Rephaim at Ashteroth-karnaim, Zuzim at Ham, Emim at Shaveh-kiriathaim, Horites in Seir to El-paran, then back to En-mishpat/Kadesh, Amalekites and Amorites at Hazazon-tamar) runs about 1,500 km from Elam by the King's Highway. The text gives no duration. I set about 6 months with a 3-month margin. This is an estimate and keeps the REGNAL_YEAR tier of the fourteenth year.

[event:evt.gen_14.sack_of_sodom] Verse 10 says the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled and fell in the bitumen pits, while the survivors fled to the hills. I read this as the defeat and kept it in the battle event. Verses 11–12 (plunder and the capture of Lot) are a separate event because they follow the battle and bring a change of subject (Lot enters the story).

[event:evt.gen_14.fugitive_reports] The fugitive (hapalit) is unnamed. Targum Pseudo-Jonathan identifies him as Og and puts the arrival on Passover eve. I follow the plain text and do not use this. Sodom to Mamre is about 63 km by road: hurry gives about 1 day.

[event:evt.gen_14.abram_pursues_to_dan] Mamre to Dan is about 244 km by road: hurry gives 4.5 days. I used this for the whole muster-and-pursuit (v14); mustering the 318 is assumed to take a few hours inside that span. If the captors travelled slowly with plunder and captives, a faster pursuer overtaking them at Dan after about 4.5 days is plausible.

[event:evt.gen_14.night_attack] v15 'divided himself against them by night': Rashi/Ramban read it as the pursuit continuing after dark, Radak as a surprise attack at midnight, Sforno as a ruse to hide small numbers. I place the attack in the night with time_of_day ASHMORET_HATICHONAH (22:00) and a 3-hour margin, covering both readings. Dan to Hobah direct is about 172 km straight (hurry about 3.5–4 days). The route via Damascus in the packet's travel tool gives 4 days; I use 4 days because the text says Hobah is 'north (left) of Damascus', so the road likely ran through the Damascus region.

[event:evt.gen_14.return_with_captives] Verse 16 does not describe the return journey but it is implied: Abram brings back goods, Lot, the women and the people, and v17 has the king of Sodom meeting him at the Valley of Shaveh. Hobah to Shaveh via Damascus is 418 km by road: walking with captives and livestock gives about 14.5 days. The text gives no duration. If the party returned by a more direct route (e.g. via Dan), it would be shorter. The margin is 3 days.

[event:evt.gen_14.melchizedek_blesses] Salem is identified with Jerusalem in the registry (Ps 76:2). The King's Valley is placed near Jerusalem (31.767, 35.236), and the Valley of Shaveh at 31.541, 35.686: the registry gives two different spots for what v17 identifies as one place. The difference does not change any date. Verses 18–20 are one scene: Melchizedek brings out bread and wine, blesses Abram and receives a tenth.
